summary: Fix run of item 'guards' after its review (accept_after_fixes). The existing guards.patch was applied in a fresh worktree; all three must_fix findings and all eight should_fix findings are dealt with, and guards.patch is rewritten (26 files, applies to a clean HEAD). (1) The Kit test in test_release_check no longer needs tools/planted_bugs to exist: it builds a temporary tree that holds the folder, a sibling file and check_release.py, and asserts payload_paths ships only the two others; it still asserts the live tree ships nothing under tools/planted_bugs. In a kit-shaped folder (payload + MANIFEST.json, 1321 files) test_release_check is now 25 OK. (2) Digest rule for the Rail Demo modules: the hold is now one shared helper, tests_integrated/seed_hold.py, used by test_desk_acts (started before an early seed too, which is how test_rail_demo's scene window was escaping it), test_context_menu and test_rail_demo's Workspace. test_rail_demo_campaign runs the real program in child processes the hold cannot reach, so its TheRuns class now skips on an edited seed and says why. On a stale seed (a comment in engineering_kernel.py): test_rail_demo 34 OK (was 4 failures), test_rail_demo_campaign OK with TheRuns skipped (was 2 failures), test_desk_acts 30 OK, test_context_menu 45 OK, test_desk_scenes 5 OK, and test_project_desk fails only Seed.test_the_seed_of_this_tree_is_current. The earlier claim is corrected below: no window test fails on the digest alone, and the campaign's twin runs are skipped, not passed, on a stale seed. (3) run.py no longer leaves a planted bug behind: plant.py writes the file's own text to a marker in the copy (tools/planted_bugs/.planted.json) before planting, refuses to plant while a marker is there, and restore() puts the file back; every run first restores and makes the seed current. Measured on a real copy: kill -9 of the run during M078's test left the marker and no test process; the next run put M078 back and gave M075 'missed' (the review saw 'caught'), and the file was byte-identical afterwards. Should-fix: one Ctrl-C now stops at once (the running tests are ended, their bugs put back and not written, exit 130; measured 1.1 s on a real bug); a missing file is 'gone' and the run goes on; any other per-bug failure is an 'error' row tried again next run; a refresh timeout is a reason, not a dead worker; a tree that cannot be made current again stops the run with exit 1 and names the bug and tree; the default --out is beside the first copy; test_record_paths is in tier 0 (tools/tiers.json, docs/CHECKS.md); test_frame's status line test asserts the parts and their order, not the words; the release note carries the same-sample caveat. A new module, test_planted_bugs (4 tests, listed in FOCUSED_MODULES on its own line), holds run.py to all this on an invented tree; against the old run.py it gave 3 failures and 1 error, now 4 OK; in a kit it skips with its reason. Every module touched or importing what was touched passes in both looks. The planted-bug numbers are the build run's (not rerun as a whole here); five guarding/other bugs rerun with the new runner were each caught by their new test.

decisions: Fix run, must_fix 2: the campaign's twins run tools/campaign.py in child processes, which the in-process hold cannot reach, and the program's own refusal of a stale seed must not be weakened. So TheRuns skips (not passes) on an edited seed, with a reason naming test_project_desk.Seed; an absent or broken seed still fails. This is a test that says why it does not run, not a pass on the digest. When the seed is current nothing changes.

Fix run, must_fix 3: the marker lives in the copy under tools/planted_bugs/ (never shipped, outside MANIFEST.json's payload), written atomically before the planted file; plant() refuses while it exists, so a leftover bug can never become the 'original'. Every run restores and makes the seed current before the first bug, and refuses to run on a tree that cannot be made current.

Fix run, should_fix 1 and 3: test processes run in a session of their own (a terminal Ctrl-C reaches only run.py, which ends them itself and discards the bug they were measuring, since a cut-off test proves nothing) and under setpriv --pdeathsig KILL where setpriv exists, so a killed run leaves no test running. Packaging runs in its own session without that signal, so it is never cut off half written. A stop for a tree error keeps the row that was measured, then exits 1.
Fix run: the 'refresh_failed' verdict in the README did not exist in the code (rows carry a 'refresh' reason); the README now describes what run.py writes, and the new 'error' verdict.

run.py makes the seed current with tools/package_graphite.py --manifest-only only, and does not record docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json again. The registry records operations and the code that serves each, not source bytes, so when LiveRecord fails on a planted bug the behaviour of the live foundation changed. M092, M094 and M095 are counted as caught that way. Re-recording the registry would hide that change.

When packaging refuses a planted tree, the bug runs on the stale seed. Every failure counts except test_project_desk.Seed.test_the_seed_of_this_tree_is_current, and the report lists the bug apart (M093, M096). The headline numbers set these two apart, and I also give the figure that counts them.

release_note: 0.8.4 checks its own tests by planting small bugs in the code and counting how many the tests catch. In the code that protects you (Kasandra's hand, the Kernel's permissions and record paths, the memory and model rules, change sets and undo, continuing work, the seed and release checks), the tests caught 30 of 53 at 0.8.2 and catch 51 now (96%); the other two make packaging refuse to build. Most of the new tests were written for these same planted bugs, so 96% says these holes are closed, not how a bug nobody has planted yet would fare; across all 131 the rate rose from 53% to 76%. A window test no longer fails only because the seed is out of date: one test says so and names the commands that fix it, and the Rail Demo scene run, which runs the program itself, says why it waits. The rerun lives in tools/planted_bugs, can be stopped and started again safely, and is never shipped.
